newsitem.title: USA: San Diego, Calif., talks on stadium falter - mayor.
newsitem.headline: San Diego, Calif., talks on stadium falter - mayor.

text.p: Efforts by San Diego's mayor to resolve a dispute with opponents of the city's $78 million stadium expansion project have faltered, a spokeswoman for the mayor said on Friday.

MaryAnne Pintar, Mayor Susan Golding's spokeswoman, said the mayor has concluded that further discussions with plaintiffs in a lawsuit opposing the Jack Murphy stadium project "would not be productive."
Pintar said opponents of the stadium project were "not willing to act in good faith," and that the matter would most likely have to be settled in court.
Pintar said the mayor no longer plans to call a special meeting of the city council to discuss negotiations.
A trial date has been set for February 20 on San Diego's expansion and renovation of Jack Murphy stadium. Opponents of the expansion are demanding that San Diego place the project on the ballot.

The National Football League said late on Thursday that it has adopted a contingency plan to move the 1998 Super Bowl from San Diego to the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, Calif., because of the legal dispute.

The league said it has entered into an option agreement with the Los Angeles Sports & Entertainment Commission and the Rose Bowl Operating Co to host the game in Pasadena should bonds needed to renovate San Diego's Jack Murphy stadium be subject to a voter referendum this spring.
